recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This image shows the spiral galaxy NGC 253, also called the Sculptor Galaxy, one of the brightest galaxies that lies beyond our Local Group. Within the Sculptor group of galaxies, NGC 253 is the brightest member. The group clusters around the south galactic pole and is therefore sometimes called the South Polar Group.

Beyond our own Local Group, the Sculptor group may be the next nearest galaxy group, at about 8 million light-years from Earth. NGC 253 is considered a starburst galaxy, meaning that stars are born, and blow up, within it at an unusually high rate.
Caroline Herschel, sister of the astronomer William Herschel, found NGC 253 on 23 September 1783, and the galaxy ranks among her major discoveries.
scale: The Sculptor group is about 8 million light-years from Earth, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: The Mosaic II camera on the Blanco 4-meter telescope observed NGC 253 through B, V and I filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter, covering visible light to the edge of near-infrared. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
